CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  November 14, 2023

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and
Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community. Meetings are held on
the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month.

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November 14, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.

City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are
compensated $438.22 per month.

(12)  ORDINANCES

  a.  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTERS 5.06 (SIDEWALK VENDING), 5.36
  (MOBILE FOOD VENDING), 8.58 (VACANT PROPERTY MAINTENANCE),
  9.65 (MEDIAN ISLANDS), 9.66 (CATALYTIC CONVERTERS), AND 9.67
  (SPEED CONTESTS); AMENDING CHAPTERS 5.14 (FILMING ACTIVITIES),
  8.13 (ADMINISTRATIVE CITATION), 9.08 (CONDUCT IN PUBLIC PLACES),
  9.18 (LOUD OR UNRULY PARTIES, GATHERINGS AND OTHER
  DISTURBANCES OF THE PEACE), 1.01 (CODE ADOPTION), 12.14
  (CAMPING AND STORAGE OF PERSONAL PROPERTY ON PUBLIC
  PROPERTY),  1.14 (MUNICIPAL  ELECTION),  2.04 (ADMINISTRATIVE
  OFFICER), 2.08 (COUNCIL MEETINGS), 2.80 (PERSONNEL RULES FOR
  CLASSIFIED AND NON-CLASSIFIED EMPLOYEES), OF THE SIGNAL HILL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO IMPROVE AND ENHANCE OPERATION OF THE CITY;
  AND FINDING THE ORDINANCE AS EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  Summary:

  In a proactive initiative to modernize the Signal Hill (“City”) Municipal Code, City
  staff and the City Attorney’s office have worked together to identify portions of
  the City’s Municipal Code requiring updates to conform with State law and
  integrate best practices. This collaborative effort has resulted in amendments
  and new additions to the City’s Municipal Code including, but not limited to, code
  enforcement, vending regulations, health and safety, and other updates tailored
  to fit the community’s evolving needs. These updates to the Municipal Code are
  presented to the City Council in one comprehensive omnibus ordinance.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain Community Safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 3  Economic & Downtown Development:  Improve the local
  economy, support local businesses, and create a vibrant
  downtown core.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure:  Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends the City Council approve the proposed changes to the Signal

  Hill Municipal Code by introducing the ordinance.

  Introduce an ordinance, entitled:

(13)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  RESOLUTION APPROVING AND ADOPTING A SIDE LETTER OF
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL AND THE SIGNAL HILL
  POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION

  Summary:

  The Signal Hill Police Department is currently experiencing a high level of
  vacancies in sworn Police Officer positions. To improve recruitment efforts,
  attract lateral Police Officer candidates, and increase retention efforts staff is
  proposing a new incentive program. The proposed program would enable a
  lateral Police Officer hire to receive credit for prior years of continuous law
  enforcement public service as a Peace Officer Standards and Training
  (P.O.S.T.) certified or P.O.S.T. approved Peace Officer for the purpose of sick
  leave, vacation leave, and longevity pay. The program also includes a proposed
  modification to the longevity pay structure in the current Signal Hill Police
  Officers’ Association (SHPOA) Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). The City
  met and conferred with the SHPOA, and mutually agreed to amend Section 36
  (Longevity Pay) of the 2021 - 2024 SHPOA MOU and implement the proposed
  Police Lateral Recruitment Incentive Program. A resolution approving the Side
  Letter of Agreement between the City and SHPOA is presented for City Council
  consideration. If approved by the City Council, the program would be
  implemented immediately and would be retroactive to July 1, 2023.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):
  Page 4 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  Goal 2: Community Safety: Maintain Community Safety by supporting public
  safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal 5:  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt the following resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND ADOPTING A SIDE LETTER OF
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL AND THE SIGNAL
  HILL POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the agreement in a form approved by
  the City Attorney.
  b.  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION VACANCY

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider opening a recruitment to fill an unscheduled
  vacancy on the Parks and Recreation Commission, to serve for the remainder of
  the vacant term through May 31, 2025.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning  Government:  Strengthen  internal
  communication, recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to
  increase the effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Declare the vacancy of one Parks and Recreation Commissioner position;
  and

  2. Authorize staff to open a recruitment seeking residents interested in serving
  as a Parks and Recreation Commissioner for the remainder of the vacant
  term through May 31, 2025. The recruitment will run from November 17,
  through December 15, 2023; and

  3. Select a date to conduct the Parks and Recreation Commissioner candidate
  interviews and appointment.
  c.  PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH TTS ENGINEERING INCORPORATED
  FOR THE 33RD STREET WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT
  (PROJECT NO. 95.22003)

  Page 5 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider authorizing the City Manager to enter into a Public
  Works Contract with TTS Engineering Incorporated (TTS) for the construction of
  the 33rd Street Water Main Replacement Project, in the amount of $2,317,861
  with a contingency up to $129,335.40. In March 2023, the City released this
  project out to bid with the original scope of work, which resulted in the rejection
  of bids due to bid irregularities. Consequently, the City revised the scope of work
  and re-released a Notice Inviting Bids (NIB) on October 13, 2023, with a bid due
  date of November 3, 2023; the City received nine bids by the deadline. Following
  review of bids, staff determined TTS is the lowest responsive and responsible
  bidder with the proper experience to perform the water main pipeline
  replacement on 33rd Street and related work identified in the NIB and contract
  documents. Subject to City Council approval of the contract award, staff would
  issue a Notice to Proceed and begin coordinating with the contractor.
  Construction of the project is estimated to start in January 2024 with completion
  within 120 working days.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure:  Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Public Works Contract with
  TTS for the construction of the 33rd Street Water Main Replacement
  Project (Project No. 95.22003), for a term of 120 working days, for a
  not-to-exceed contract amount of $2,317,861, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney; and

  2. Authorize the Public Works Director to utilize a contingency of up to
  $129,335.40 to accommodate additional scope of work in the event of
  changed or unforeseen conditions and utilize remaining American
  Rescue Plan Act funds, for a total construction budget of $2,447,196.40.
  d.  DISPLAY OF COMMEMORATIVE FLAGS

  Summary:

  Per Resolution No. 2021-10-6442, the City Council will consider the display of
  commemorative flags for the upcoming year.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.

  Page 6 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  Recommendations:

  1. Consider the list of commemorative flags to be displayed for calendar year
  2024.

  2. Direct staff to return to a future City Council meeting with a resolution
  memorializing the commemorative flags to be displayed for calendar year
  2024.
(14)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following Consent Calendar items are expected to be routine and
  non-controversial. Items will be acted upon by the Council at one time without
  discussion. Any item may be removed by a Council Member for discussion.
  a.  WAIVE THE READING OF ORDINANCES IN FULL AND AUTHORIZE
  READING BY TITLE ONLY

  Summary:

  The recommended action waives reading of ordinances in full and authorizes
  reading by title only. The purpose of this item is to streamline the City Council
  meeting process, avoid unnecessary delay and allow more time for substantive
  discussion of items on the agenda.
  Recommendation:

  Waive the reading of all ordinances. Wherein the titles appear on the public
  agenda; said titles shall be determined to have been read by title, and further
  reading is waived.
  b.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2023-10-1544, AMENDING SECTION
  1.02.010 AND SECTION 1.02.020 OF CHAPTER 1.02 OF THE SIGNAL HILL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE CITY SEAL, AND ADOPTION OF A
  RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A POLICY FOR THE USE OF THE
  COMMEMORATIVE ANNIVERSARY CITY SEAL AND LOGO FOR THE CITY’S
  CENTENNIAL YEAR

  Summary:

  Ordinance No. 2023-10-1544 amending section 1.02 of Chapter 1.02 of the
  Signal Hill Municipal Code (SHMC) to effectuate the adoption of the new City
  seal was introduced at the City Council meeting of October 24, 2023, and is now
  presented for City Council adoption. As required by SHMC section 1.02.150,
  staff prepared a Resolution establishing a policy governing the use of the
  Commemorative Anniversary City Seal and Logo for City Council approval.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,

  Page 7 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt Ordinance No. 2023-10-1544, entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SIGNAL HILL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 1.02.010
  AND SECTION 1.02.020 OF CHAPTER 1.02 OF THE SIGNAL
  HILL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE CITY SEAL

  2. Adopt a Resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SIGNAL HILL, CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING A POLICY FOR
  THE USE OF THE COMMEMORATIVE ANNIVERSARY CITY
  SEAL AND LOGO FOR THE CITY’S CENTENNIAL YEAR
  c.  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT  WITH  LONG  BEACH  ANIMAL
  CONTROL SERVICES BUREAU

  Summary:

  On June 28, 2022, the City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a
  contract services agreement with the City of Long Beach Animal Control
  Services Bureau (LBACS) for a two-year term from July 1, 2022, through June
  30, 2024, with an option to extend the contract for two year terms, up to two
  terms maximum. The annual contract cost was for an amount not to exceed
  $122,422. In July 2023, LBACS informed the City that the costs for the second
  year of the contract would be increased by $25,261, due to its implementation of
  a new service delivery model, Compassion Saves, which has led to the
  reduction of animal euthanasia. The proposed new agreement also includes
  increased engagement efforts to the community, such as quarterly pet adoption
  presentations; and education and low-cost resources promoting responsible pet
  ownership. Staff is requesting City Council authorization to execute the new
  contract services agreement from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, in the amount
  not-to-exceed $147,683. If the City extends future terms of the contract, up to
  two terms maximum, the contract costs could increase by a not-to-exceed
  Consumer Price Index (CPI) maximum adjustment of 8% per year.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.

  Page 8 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Contract Services Agreement
  with the City of Long Beach for animal care services, from July 1, 2022,
  through June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed $147,683 (year 2
  cost), in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute future amendments extending the
  term by two additional years, up to two terms maximum, with an annual
  cost increase not-to-exceed a CPI adjustment of 8%; and

  3. Adopt a resolution entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND
  AUTHORIZING BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2023-24
  d.  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MVP SECURITY SYSTEMS
  INCORPORATED FOR THE ACCESS CONTROL SYSTEM PROJECT

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider approving a Contract Services Agreement with
  MVP Security Systems, Incorporated (MVP) to provide Access Control Systems
  (ACS) software and partial hardware upgrades at the Police Station, City Hall,
  and the Library, in the amount of $122,865 with a 10% contingency up to
  $12,286. The City released a Request for Proposals (RFP) for these services on
  September 15, 2023, with a proposal due date of October 20, 2023; the City
  received five proposals by the deadline. Following staff review of proposals and
  interviews, MVP was the highest ranked firm. Based on the evaluation process,
  staff believes MVP is the best qualified firm with the proper experience to
  provide access control system upgrades and software system support. If
  approved by the City Council, staff anticipates MVP would complete the system
  upgrades within six months from the contract start date. MVP would also provide
  a three-year system service support plan.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure:  Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Contract Services Agreement
  with MVP for the Access Control System Project (Project No. 90.21001),
  for a term of six months for a not-to-exceed contract amount of $122,865,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  Page 9 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  2. Authorize the Public Works Director to utilize a contingency of up to 10%
  ($12,286) to accommodate additional scope of work in the event of
  changed or unforeseen conditions, for a total project budget of $135,151.
  e.  PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE OF OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY SELECTIVE
  TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM GRANT AND ADOPTION OF
  RESOLUTION APPROVING BUDGET AMENDMENT

  Summary:

  The Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) Selective Traffic Enforcement Program
  (STEP) awarded the Signal Hill Police Department a $90,000 grant. The City’s
  awarded STEP grant funding would allow the Police Department to carry out
  traffic safety enforcement targeting primary collision factors, including driving
  under the influence, that contribute to traffic collisions. The grant would offset
  the cost of police overtime, training, and related supplies. Staff recommends the
  City Council adopt a resolution accepting the grant and authorizing a budget
  adjustment to increase grant revenue by $30,000.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the Police Chief to accept grant funding through the OTS STEP
  grant.

  2. Adopt a resolution, entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL, CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED
  BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-24
  f.  PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH VICON ENTERPRISE INCORPORATED
  FOR THE FUEL STATION CANOPY REPLACEMENT PROJECT (90.17015)

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider entering into a Public Works Contract with Vicon
  Enterprise Incorporated for the Fuel Station Canopy Replacement Project, in the
  amount of $445,000 with a 10% contingency up to $44,500. The City released a
  Notice Inviting Bids (NIB) for these services on September 21, 2023, with a bid
  due date of October 26, 2023; the City received three bids by the deadline.
  Following review of bids, staff determined Vicon Enterprise Incorporated is the
  lowest responsive and responsible contractor with the proper experience to
  perform the scope of work for the Fuel Station Canopy Replacement Project.

  Page 10 of 12
 City Council  Regular  November 14, 2023

  Subject to City Council approval of the contract award, staff would issue a
  Notice to Proceed and begin coordinating with the contractor. Construction of
  the project is estimated to start in December 2023, with completion within 90
  working days.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Public Works Contract with
  Vicon Enterprise Incorporated for construction of the Fuel Station Canopy
  Replacement Project (Project No. 90.17015), for a term of 90 working
  days, for a not-to-exceed contract amount of $445,000, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney; and

  2. Authorize the Public Works Director to utilize a contingency of up to 10%
  ($44,500) to accommodate additional scope of work in the event of
  changed or unforeseen conditions, for a total construction budget of
  $489,500.

  g.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED NOVEMBER 14, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the
  prior warrant register and warrants to be released upon City Council approval.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize payment of the Warrant Register dated November 14, 2023.
  h.  APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES

  Summary:

  Regular Meeting of October 24, 2023.
  Recommendation:

  Approve the meeting minutes.

(16)  ADJOURNMENT

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to a special meeting of the Signal Hill City Council
  on Tuesday, December 5, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. The next regular meeting of the Signal Hill
  City Council will be held on Tuesday, December 12, 2023, at 7:00 p.m., in the Council
  Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal Hill, CA 90755. There will be no
  regular meeting of the Signal Hill City Council on November 28, 2023.
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
